EmailTemplate.subject: Join us for a Blood Drive
EmailTemplate.textOnly:
Dear [BPL Name],
**Add personal introduction**
Thank you so much for your support and commitment to increasing awareness in the LGBTQ+ community about blood donation and increasing the diversity of the blood supply!
Did you know that in May 2023, the FDA lifted the sexual orientation deferral, replacing it with the Individual Donor Assessment (IDA)? This change has made the blood donation process more inclusive. On August 7, 2023, the American Red Cross was the first major blood bank to implement these changes, allowing more donors to participate in their lifesaving efforts!
The American Red Cross has been working for many years toward achieving an inclusive blood donation process that treats all potential donors with equality and respect while maintaining the safety of the nation’s blood supply. The rich diversity and intersectionality in the LGBTQ+ community also supports our sickle cell and Latino initiatives. For example, diverse populations are essential in addressing the ongoing demand for blood, particularly type O, which is frequently in short supply and urgently needed by hospitals. Notably, 51% of Black or African American individuals and 57% of Hispanic or Latino individuals have type O blood.
As a leader in your community, you have the opportunity to make a meaningful difference by hosting a Red Cross blood drive during the following months.
March is Bisexual Health Awareness Month
Encourage blood donations this month in recognition of Bisexual Health Awareness Month, which highlights the health disparities and unique challenges faced by bisexual individuals. Let’s unite as a community and organize a blood drive to ensure that blood is available for those in need.
Harvey Milk Day is in May
Invite donors to give blood in honor of Harvey Milk Day, celebrated in May. Harvey Milk was California's first openly gay elected official and a dedicated advocate for LGBTQ+ rights. Hosting a blood drive is a wonderful way to bring the community together in celebration of compassion, diversity, and unity.
Pride Month
Consider organizing a Red Cross blood drive to commemorate Pride in June or anytime, celebrating the LGBTQ+ community. This is an excellent opportunity to emphasize community strength—what better way to celebrate than by saving lives through blood donation.
October is LGBTQ+ History Month
October is recognized as LGBTQ+ History Month, and it also includes National Coming Out Day which promotes the visibility and sharing of experiences among individuals in the LGBTQ+ community. This is a perfect opportunity to come together as a community by organizing a blood drive. This initiative also supports patients battling blood disorders like sickle cell disease, those needing platelets for cancer treatment, individuals recovering from traumatic injuries, and many others in need.
Let’s work together to schedule your drive and provide hope to those in need!
Best regards,
[Your Name]
[Your Title]
[Your Email]
